summary: The root أزز (azz) primarily describes a state of agitation, excitement, or intense provocation. It can refer to a strong urging or incitement, often with a sense of disturbance or unrest.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: أَزَّتِ القِدْرُ, (S, K,) or البُرْمَةُ, (A,) aor اَزُزَ (S, K) and اَزِزَ, (K,) inf. n. أَزِيزٌ (S, A, K) and أَزٌّ and أَزَازٌ, (K,) The cooking-pot made a sound in boiling: (S, accord. to an explanation there given of the inf. n.; and A:) or boiled: (S:) or boiled vehemently; (K;) as also [written with the disjunctive alif اِيتَّزَّت ], (S, K,) inf. n. ٱئْتِزَازٌ; (S;) and, (K,) inf. N. تَأَزُّزٌ: (TA:) or all signify it boiled not vehemently.
ائتزّت القِدْرُ: see 1. هُوَ يَأْتَزُّ مِنْ كَ َا He becomes angry, and distressed, and disquieted or disturbed, by reason of such a thing. (A, TA.)
أَزِيزٌ inf. n. of 1. Sharpness; syn. حِدَّةٌ. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
